decisions.title: Web framework and hosting
decisions.body: Next.js stays the web pick for its ecosystem and because Claude Code knows it best. It deploys to Cloudflare Workers through the OpenNext adapter (Next.js 16.2.3+), so it fits the free, commercial-OK default stack. Vercel Hobby is non-commercial, so Vercel is only an option on Pro.

decisions.title: One booking tool
decisions.body: Cal.com Free covers customer interviews and sales calls in one account, with a free Attio sync. It replaces Google appointment schedules in the Discover track.

decisions.title: Meeting notes
decisions.body: Fathom Free is the default, Meetily handles healthcare/PHI calls locally, and Gemini Meet notes are an extra only if your account has them.

decisions.title: One build workflow
decisions.body: Superpowers runs the plan-test-build loop. Spec Kit only writes spec documents. Disable other planners in the same repo.

decisions.title: Jobs
decisions.body: Cloudflare Queues by default. Inngest only for multi-step LLM workflows.

decisions.title: Newsletters
decisions.body: Substack for you, Kit for products. Start with Substack.

decisions.title: Sending mail for outreach
decisions.body: Zoho Mail Forever Free has no IMAP or SMTP access, so sequencers can't send through it. Apollo's free plan connects Gmail only. Put outbound mailboxes on a separate lookalike domain in Google Workspace when outbound starts, and keep Zoho or Cloudflare routing for the main domain.

decisions.title: Payouts
decisions.body: Dodo pays out in USD/GBP/EUR only. Route payouts to a bank account that accepts foreign inward remittance and keep the FIRA for GST export proof. Verify the setup with your CA.

decisions.title: Healthcare clients
decisions.body: None of the free plans in the default stack signs a HIPAA BAA. Before PHI arrives: AWS (self-serve BAA, Bedrock HIPAA-eligible) or Google Cloud (self-serve BAA), Neon Scale, Sentry Business, PostHog Boost or higher. Anthropic and OpenAI BAAs go through sales.

notes.title: Bypass mode on native Windows has no sandbox
notes.body: Claude Code's Bash sandbox runs in WSL2, not on native Windows. If you skip permission prompts there, every command runs unisolated. Use auto mode with allow and deny rules, and open untrusted repos inside WSL2 with /sandbox.

notes.title: Keep client and health data off free AI tiers
notes.body: Gemini API free-tier terms forbid sending sensitive or personal data and require the paid tier for apps offered in the EEA. Consumer AI subscriptions carry no HIPAA BAA. Use paid, no-training endpoints for customer data. Claude Max API credits may power your own products.

notes.title: Docker Desktop licence on a company laptop
notes.body: Docker Desktop is free only for companies under 250 employees and under $10M revenue, and on a work machine that test applies to your employer. Docker Engine inside WSL2 has no licence test.

notes.title: Pin GitHub Actions and Python deps
notes.body: Trivy's GitHub Action tags were hijacked on 19-20 March 2026 (CVE-2026-33634), and LiteLLM 1.82.7-1.82.8 on PyPI were credential stealers on 24 March 2026. Pin actions to post-incident commit SHAs, pin package versions, and run zizmor on your workflows. If you ever installed those LiteLLM versions, remove litellm_init.pth and rotate secrets.

notes.title: One free Workers quota for everything
notes.body: On Cloudflare's free plan, your MCP server, API, AI Gateway logs and site share 100k requests a day. Move to Workers Paid ($5/mo) or split accounts as traffic grows.

phases.title: Secure your machine
steps: Turn off bypass permissions in Claude Code; use auto mode with allow and deny rules.
Install and sign in to the GitHub CLI: gh auth login.
On a company laptop, check the Docker Desktop licence test; otherwise use Docker Engine in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04.
Install uv standalone and keep one global Python.
Remove MCP servers and plugins you don't use; each one costs context.

phases.title: Claude Code core
steps: Install the official LSP plugins for TypeScript and Python.
Install Superpowers as your one build workflow.
Add the Playwright CLI and skills, Context7 and Exa.
Install Scoop (user scope) and the CLI set: lazygit, delta, fd, fzf, bat, zoxide.
Set up Infisical so secrets never sit in plaintext .env files.

phases.title: Free accounts
steps: Create accounts on GitHub, Cloudflare (Workers, R2, DNS, Email Routing, Web Analytics), Neon, Resend, Sentry, PostHog and UptimeRobot.
Register your domain at Cloudflare Registrar.
Get a Gemini API key for prototypes only; claim Claude Max API credits in the Console for products.

phases.title: Product stack
steps: Scaffold with Better-T-Stack: pnpm + Turborepo, Next.js 16.2.3+, Hono, Drizzle on Neon and Expo. Add the Electron app by hand with electron-builder, because Electron isn't a Better-T-Stack option.
Deploy the web app with @opennextjs/cloudflare, and the API and MCP server on Workers with the OAuth provider.
Put Langfuse tracing and promptfoo evals in CI from day one.
Use EAS free builds for mobile and run the Play Console closed test (12 testers, 14 days).
Ship desktop as MSIX through the Microsoft Store for free signing.

phases.title: Money and legal (India)
steps: Onboard to Dodo Payments as an individual. Use Razorpay for INR customers and Skydo or Wise for service invoices.
Keep invoices and books in Zoho Books Free, register on Udyam, and have a CA review GST and Section 58 before the first export invoice.
Adopt Common Paper templates, DocuSeal for e-signature, and Probo for a trust page.
File the trademark (classes 9 and 42) once the name is final.

phases.title: Sell
steps: Set up Attio Free as the CRM and Apollo for data and sequences, sending from a separate domain with DMARC.
Use Cal.com Free for interviews and sales, Fathom Free for notes, and Meetily for calls with health data.
Build an Astro site and Starlight docs on Cloudflare, with Search Console and Ahrefs Webmaster Tools.
Add Chatwoot, UserJot and Supademo when users arrive. Launch on Show HN, Product Hunt and Peerlist.

phases.title: Run and grow
steps: Run Obsidian as your second brain, GitHub Projects as the backlog, Super Productivity for daily planning and Reclaim Lite for calendars.
Post natively on LinkedIn, schedule with Buffer Free, and start a Substack.
Every Friday, spend 45 minutes on Inoreader, Hugging Face Daily Papers, AINews, Simon Willison and Import AI.
